definitions.principal: Collected whole menu makes this a principal food family.
definitions.co_main: One of a small number of principal food families.
definitions.mixed: Target dish exists amid broad menu; principal family uncertain.
definitions.secondary: Side/set/lunch/isolated menu among another dominant family.
definitions.adjacent: Related food but not pork cutlet.
definitions.outside_scope: Other noodle family or uncertain broad noodle screen; NOT evidence that current hot-noodle request fails.
definitions.no_evidence: No target evidence in collected menu/name screening; not proof of non-sale.
definitions.style: Conservative cuisine-style proxy for scenario labels, not latent flavour identity.

scope.cutlet: Pork cutlet as main food; Japanese/Western style only independently confirmed labels, both/mixed and not-established explicit.
scope.ramen_korean_hot_noodle: Ramen and Korean hot broth noodles; not all hot soup noodles. Chinese/Vietnamese noodles/udon/other noodle-screen matches outside this comparative axis remain outside_scope.

limits: Real catalogue menu audit; labels define hypothetical scenario relevance, not observed human preferences.
No model result was opened while making these labels.
Keyword screening can miss unnamed target foods. No-evidence and outside-scope are not confirmed negatives.
Style masks deliberately leave unsupported restaurants unclassified; the 12 cutlet strict style labels come from an earlier score-blind contextual review audit.
Japanese vs Korean noodle style correlates with ingredients/preparation/price. It is not an isolated latent-vector semantic dimension.
